title: Test-Time Deep Thinking to Explore Implicit Rules

problem.claim: Agents fail in environments governed by implicit rules that must be inferred through interaction, leading to repetitive trial-and-error loops and task failure.

gap.claim: Deep reasoning trajectories are difficult and unstable to evaluate, obstructing effective training.

contributions.claim: TTExplore uses a thinker component to infer implicit rules from interaction history and guide an actor.
A reinforcement learning pipeline uses task-level scores as indirect rewards and retains one thinking node per trajectory to address intermediate-reasoning evaluation and reward sparsity.
The authors train a specialized 7B model called Exp-Thinker.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce a novel and stable reinforcement learning pipeline.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five text-based embodied tasks report that TTExplore with Exp-Thinker improves baseline agent performance by an average of 14–19 points.
The authors report that these results demonstrate the effectiveness of explicitly reasoning about implicit rules.

narrative_sequence.summary: Intelligent agents are becoming increasingly important as LLMs advance.
Agents struggle with implicit rules and can enter repetitive trial-and-error loops that cause task failure.
TTExplore adds a thinker that analyzes interaction history to infer implicit rules and guide an actor.
A stable reinforcement learning pipeline uses indirect task-level rewards and one thinking node per trajectory, producing the specialized Exp-Thinker model.
Across five text-based embodied tasks, the system is reported to improve baseline performance by an average of 14–19 points.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates implicit-rule inference into a thinker component that guides an actor.

interpretation.claim: Separating analysis from action may help agents convert interaction history into reusable behavioral guidance.

application.claim: Use a dedicated inference or planning component to summarize hidden constraints before selecting actions in partially observed environments.

exception.claim: This lesson may not apply when hidden constraints cannot be inferred reliably from available interaction history.

source_observation.claim: The training pipeline uses task-level scores as indirect rewards and retains one thinking node per trajectory.

interpretation.claim: Sparse or unstable intermediate-reasoning supervision can be bypassed by optimizing against reliable end-task outcomes.

application.claim: For tasks with accurate outcome scores but difficult intermediate evaluation, train using outcome-level rewards and a compact reasoning trace.

exception.claim: This approach depends on accurate task-level scores and may be unsuitable when outcome scoring is unreliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five tasks, baseline systems, evaluation protocol, or score definitions.
The abstract does not provide per-task results, variance, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement learning algorithm, dataset, or training details.
